To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The mixed carbonate-siciliclastic Weißenegger Formation records three deposicional sequences corresponding approximately to TB 2.2, TB 2,3 and TB 2,4.

the Weißenegg Formation (Styrian Basin; Austria) records three depositional sequence corresponding approximately to the Tethyan global cycles TB 2.2, TB 2,4 and TB 25 and that the sea level fluctuations were of the same order as those of the global cycles.

the Middle Miocene (Sarmatian) Weißenegg Formation records three deposi-tional sequences, that the lowstand systems tract consists of lignite deposits, that transgres-sive systems tracts contain distinct layers of nodules which are interpreted as hardground for-merers, and that the (late)highstand systems tracts consist of shallowing upwards siliclastic parase-quences terminated by bank of rhodolites and occasionally by carbonate highstand wedges.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the recognition of the stratigraphical and palaeogeographical effects of sea-level fluctuations and with the recognition of fourth-order sea-level fluctuations.
the recognition of sea-level fluctuations in the order of tens of meters, which are superimposed on the global cycles of the Middle Miocene.
the recognition of sequence stratigraphical concepts in mixed carbonate-siliclatic depositional systems and with the interpretation of their depositional and diagenetic history.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Weißenegg Formation is a mixed carbonate-sliciciclastic sequence stratigraphic unit, recording the interplay of sea-level fluctuations, sediment supply and tectonics.
the sequence stratigraphic framework is well defined, and that it is possible to identify the major sea-level fluctuations and their effects on the depositional system.
the depositional sequences of the Weißenegg (allogenic) Formation record the response of a shallow marine carbonate-siliclastic mixed system to the global sea-level cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Weißenegg Formation represents a mixed carbonate-sicliciclastic depositional system with a strong influence of tectonic activity and sea-level fluctuations on the depositional pattern.
the Weißenegg Formation represents a complex mixed carbonate-silici-clastic depositional system, which is dominated by siliciclastic deposition.
sea-level fluctuations of the order of 30 m and superimposed fourth order sea-level fluctuations of a few meters amplitude are recorded in the studied succession.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Weißenegg Formation is not a simple, shallow water, mixed carbonate-siliclatic succession, but that it contains a complex stratigraphical record of sea-level fluctuations.
sea-level fluctuations were superimposed by fourth-order sea-level fluctuations of the order of several meters.
sequence stratigraphic models for siliciclastic systems are not applicable to mixed carbonate-silicticlastic systems.
